name: Scarface

pitch_detail.notes: Broken, relatively clean rock off the gully start; potential for loose/breaking holds warrants care.
A sustained, steep hand crack with big exposure — the route's standout, signature pitch.
Finger cracks past loose rock, then a leftward traverse along a ledge studded with unstable blocks.
The most hazard-prone pitch: large loose blocks lead to a hand crack above a slab beneath a big roof.
Pitches 5 and 6: blockier, more solid finishing pitches lead to the summit ridge.

rappel_detail.notes: Below the rappel it is a scree and talus scramble worked rightward — clockwise around the peak, roughly south then west — back into the basin and the packs at the base of the west face. Terrain under the horn is low-angle enough that some parties downclimb it instead of rappelling.
rappel_detail.anchor: A natural horn wrapped in webbing / in-situ slings on the east side of the summit block. No bolts. It is re-slung periodically because it is the standard anchor for every CBR route that tops out here, so what you find will be a mix of ages.
hazards: The upper pitches and the ground around the summit block are loose and lichen-covered — the reason parties are advised to stay roped rather than solo across to the anchor
Single natural anchor on a high-traffic descent: inspect the webbing and add or replace your own before loading it
rappel_detail.station: From the top of the route, scramble across to the east side of the summit block; the slung horn is on that side and the rappel drops eastward. If you skip the balanced-rock boulder problem you can bypass the block entirely and never touch this anchor.

rappels: Finish over the top and take the standard Colchuck Balanced Rock descent: one rappel of about 30 m east off a slung horn on the summit block, then scree clockwise around the peak. To bail low, rappel the route from natural anchors and the fixed pitons with a 60 m rope.
descent_text: Scarface tops out near the other West Face-area routes and shares Colchuck Balanced Rock's standard summit descent: class 3-4 scrambling around the right side of the true summit block (avoiding the balanced boulder) down to a sandy scree/talus gully, descended clockwise back around the peak to the base (45 min-1hr). A short section near the top is sometimes eased with an optional single ~30m rappel off a slung horn on the east side (natural anchor) instead of downclimbing. No full rappel of the route itself is required under normal conditions.
approach: From the Stuart Lake Trailhead (FS Road 7601 off Icicle Creek Road), follow the Colchuck Lake Trail (#1599) — 4 miles, 2,280 ft gain, crossing Mountaineer Creek on a log bridge at 1.5 miles, bearing left at the Lake Stuart Trail junction, finishing with a boulder-moraine climb to the outlet (2.5-3 hours). Top off water here. Head toward the lake's south/east side onto the cairned Aasgard Pass climbers' trail, gaining talus/heather to about 400 ft above the lake (30-40 min, watch for wet snow into July), then cut climber's-left through dense slide-alder/heather brush (15-20 minutes) to the base gully system. Scarface climbs the gully just left of the West Face route's start; this terrain is very loose and exposed, so extra care with rope-up/spacing is warranted through the final approach scramble. Total trailhead-to-base time runs about 3.5-4 hours, in line with neighboring routes.
overview: Scarface climbs a gully system to the left of the West Face, established by Colin B. and Nate F. in August 2010. It's roughly 1,200 ft (Grade III) over 5+ pitches, with a standout second pitch of sustained, steep hand-crack climbing and big exposure; upper pitches are blockier and more solid than the lower, looser sections.
beta: P1-2: relatively clean, though loose/breaking rock is still possible. P2 has a sustained steep hand crack with awesome exposure. P3: a tempting finger crack directly above the belay has two large sharp flakes to its left that could cut the rope or fall on the belayer; the leftward traverse above is simple but must be done delicately due to numerous loose blocks (fist to cooler size). P4: several large loose blocks between the fixed piton at the start and the left edge of a large roof, including one thigh-sized block next to the hand crack above the slab; cleaner above and around the roof. P5+: finishing pitches are blocky and less loose.
fa: Colin B. and Nate F., August 15, 2010
face: West face — up the gully left of the West Face route, several hundred feet right of the old Northwest Buttress line
